subject: Recap: Finlytics discovery — pricing & batching assumptions
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@finlytics.co>, Tom Gallagher <tom.gallagher@finlytics.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Finlytics discovery — pricing & batching assumptions

Hi Samantha / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + next steps so we’re aligned. TL;DR: we need confirmation on token volumes, budget range, and how much latency vs unit-cost tradeoff you want us to optimize for (batching / concurrency) so we can produce a concrete per-1M-token estimate and a MAP.

Call recap (short):
- Use case: real-time credit decisioning + short-form explanations in the UI (mostly chat style prompts). Some batch re-runs for model audits.
- Current estimate you gave on the call: ~50M inference tokens/month today, planning to scale to ~200M in 12 months if latency and cost align.
- Target budget range you mentioned on the call: ~$3k–$6k/month initially (pilot); long-term budget TBD depending on unit economics.
- Prospect target: you asked for a target $/1M tokens target in the $5–$8 range — we noted that tradeoffs exist (reserved capacity, quantization, batching, and caching).

Key technical assumptions we’ll use unless you tell us otherwise:
- Typical prompt + response length: ~60–120 tokens (average 80 tokens).
- Traffic pattern: continuous interactions during business hours with predictable bursts after batch jobs and evening retries. Expect sustained baseline with 2–3x short bursts.
- Latency SLO: ~300ms for UI chat (soft); willing to accept up to 600ms in rare bursts if cost drops materially.
- Batching approach: we assume continuous batching (micro-batching) with a short batch window (10–30ms) to preserve latency while enabling some utilization effects.

What we need from you to finalize a numbers-backed quote:
1) Confirm monthly token volumes split (inference vs embedding vs audit re-runs).
2) Confirm hard latency targets and acceptable tail (p95/p99) so we can size concurrency.
3) Confirm target $/1M tokens if the $5–$8 range is still relevant — or give a max allowable cost.

Next steps (proposal timeline):
- We’ll send a pricing estimate + MAP with two options: Hosted (pay-as-you-go) and Dedicated (reserved capacity) by EOD tomorrow, based on the assumptions above and a worked example for 50M -> 200M growth.
- Can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up mid-week to walk the estimate with your procurement/legal folks if helpful?

Attachments I’ll include: draft MAP and a pricing worksheet for worked examples (spreadsheet).

Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das

Subject: Re: Recap: Finlytics discovery — pricing & batching assumptions

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the clear recap. Couple clarifications from our side:

1) Volumes: current production (inference tokens) ~50M/month. Embeddings are separate — roughly 8–12M/month today for semantic search maintenance. Audit re-runs are sporadic but could add ~10–15M tokens/month during monthly compliance windows.
2) Growth: if we get latency under 400ms p95 and costs < $8 / 1M tokens, we’re comfortable committing to pilot expansion toward ~200M/month over the next 12 months.
3) Budget: Pilot budget is flexible (we landed on $3k–$6k/month above), but procurement needs a clear per-1M-token unit so they can model NPV for the FY.

On batching / concurrency — two questions: 1) how does continuous batching affect p95 latency for chat-style requests (is 300ms realistic?), and 2) can you provide a worked example that shows cost per 1M tokens under conservative vs optimized batching assumptions?

If you can include that worked example in the pricing worksheet that would be ideal. Also copying Tom (ops) so he can weigh in on acceptable tail latency.

Samantha Ortiz
Head of Product | Finlytics
samantha.ortiz@finlytics.co
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Recap: Finlytics discovery — pricing & batching assumptions

Samantha — quick technical worked example and notes below (I’ll attach the calc sheet). I mirrored the assumptions Priyom listed and used the two batching profiles you asked about.

Assumptions used (conservative / optimized):
- Avg tokens per request: 80
- Requests per month (50M tokens): ~625k requests (50,000,000 / 80)
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline + 2x short bursts (peak concurrency factor = 2.5)

Profile A — conservative (minimal batching to preserve latency):
- Batch window: 30ms (micro-batching)
- Effective avg batch size: ~4 requests
- Avg end-to-end p95 latency: ~320–380ms (includes queueing + compute)
- Cost drivers: lower utilization → higher $/1M tokens
- Estimated cost: $8.25 / 1M tokens (hosted, default kernel, no quantization)

Profile B — optimized (aggressive micro-batching + q4 quantized model):
- Batch window: 20ms with adaptive batching (holds short to form batches but releases on latency threshold)
- Effective avg batch size: ~9 requests during baseline, larger during bursts (gives better GPU utilization)
- Avg end-to-end p95 latency: ~280–350ms (p95 depends on tail arrival patterns)
- Cost drivers: better kernel utilization, quantization (Q4_0) → reduced token compute cost
- Estimated cost: $5.50 / 1M tokens (hosted, with suggested batching/quantization profile)

Notes on concurrency & Sizing:
- To meet ~300ms p95 with continuous batching you need: enough concurrent pipelines to absorb burst factor (~2.5x) and small batch windows (10–30ms). This favors more smaller instances with autoscaling that reacts to request queues rather than very few giant machines.
- Reserved capacity (Dedicated) can reduce effective $/1M tokens further but requires commit; we can model a 6–12 month commit vs pay-as-you-go in the attached spreadsheet.

I attached a worked example (spreadsheet) with step-by-step calc: arrival rate → batch size distribution → tokens/sec → estimated cost/1M for both profiles. Happy to walk through it in a short tech call if helpful.

—Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
